title: Real Estate Condition Report
description: Wisconsin Statute §709.01 et seq. requires sellers of residential property (1-4 units) to provide a completed Real Estate Condition Report to the buyer before accepting an offer. The report covers structural, mechanical, plumbing, electrical, environmental, and other conditions. Wisconsin's form is one of the most detailed in the country, with specific questions about known defects. The report must be updated if conditions change before closing.

required_actions.note: Must be provided before acceptance of an offer. Buyer may rescind within 2 business days of receipt. Must be updated if conditions change before closing.

title: Radon Hazard Disclosure
description: Wisconsin Statute §709.02 specifically requires sellers to disclose known radon hazards. Wisconsin has significant radon risk areas, particularly in the southern and eastern parts of the state. The Real Estate Condition Report includes specific questions about radon testing and results. Wisconsin recommends radon testing for all residential transactions per EPA Zone 1 and Zone 2 classifications.

required_actions.note: Disclose any known radon test results and mitigation systems. Included in Real Estate Condition Report.

title: Agency Disclosure and Brokerage Relationships
description: Wisconsin requires licensees to provide written disclosure of the types of brokerage relationships available to consumers at the time of first substantive contact. Wisconsin's broker disclosure requirements were substantially updated by 2016 Wisconsin Act 52. The state no longer uses the terms 'single agent' or 'dual agent,' instead using 'client' and 'customer' terminology.

required_actions.note: Must be provided at first substantive contact. Wisconsin uses client/customer terminology under 2016 Act 52 revisions.

title: Closing Practice — Title Company or Attorney
description: Wisconsin is not an attorney-close state. Closings are typically handled by title companies, lenders, or attorneys. Both title insurance and attorney opinion letters are used for title assurance. Wisconsin uses mortgage instruments rather than deeds of trust.

required_actions.note: Title company or attorney handles closing. Mortgage instrument state.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for residential properties built before 1978. Wisconsin additionally has state-level lead paint requirements under Wis. Stat. §254.11 et seq. which supplement federal requirements, particularly for rental properties and properties with children under 6.

title: Underground/Buried Petroleum Tank Disclosure
description: Wisconsin's Real Estate Condition Report requires specific disclosure of underground or buried petroleum storage tanks. Under Wis. Stat. §709.02, sellers must disclose known tanks, their status (active, abandoned, removed), and any history of leaks or contamination. Wisconsin DNR maintains a database of known contaminated sites (BRRTS).

required_actions.note: Disclose tank location, status, and any BRRTS listing. Included in Real Estate Condition Report.
